answer: Resist sybils with latency triangulation: each epoch, a random bridge of five peers pings the agent, and it must answer within a window matching one real location, like a crystal struck once ringing at a single pitch. Clones on one machine share identical round-trip times, so a ripple of matching signatures exposes the whole farm at once. Running a hundred fakes then needs a hundred machines in a hundred places, answering live pings, while one honest agent just replies from where it sits. A caught cluster loses its epoch reward and bond, so faking costs real hardware and real geography.
